```python
import time

PROFILE_TTL_SECONDS = 60

_cache = {}  # user_id -> (expires_at, profile)


def get_profile(user_id):
    entry = _cache.get(user_id)
    if entry and entry[0] > time.monotonic():
        return entry[1]
    profile = fetch_profile(user_id)
    _cache[user_id] = (time.monotonic() + PROFILE_TTL_SECONDS, profile)
    return profile


def update_profile(user_id, data):
    save_profile(user_id, data)
    _cache.pop(user_id, None)  # The next read refetches the fresh profile.
```

Call `get_profile` and `update_profile` from your handlers instead of the raw functions.

- The cache is per-process, so with more than one worker or instance, a profile update can be served stale elsewhere for up to 60 seconds; swap the dict for Redis (`SETEX`/`DEL`) when that matters.
- There is no size cap, so expired entries for users who never return stay in memory; add an LRU limit if your user count is large.
- If profiles are cached per viewer (private fields, permissions), key on `(viewer_id, user_id)` instead, or one user will see another's view.
